8. Damage, Wounds, Death, and Capture
Wounds

Hit points represent endurance, luck, armor deflection, and minor injury. Wounds represent lasting trauma. A creature makes a Wound save when it drops to 0 HP, suffers damage equal to at least half its maximum HP from one source, or is struck by an effect marked Maiming. The save is Constitution, DC 10 or half the triggering damage, whichever is higher.
Wound Outcome
No lasting Wound.
Gain one Wound. Each Wound imposes -1 on Constitution saves and maximum Hit Dice recovered per long rest.
Gain one Wound and roll on the Injury table.
Three Wounds
Character is Critically Wounded: Speed -10 ft., cannot regain full HP, and dies on the next failed Wound save.
At 0 HP, a character is Unconscious and makes death saves at the start of each turn: 10+ success, 9- failure, three of either resolves the state.
An action and DC 10 Medicine check stabilizes a dying creature. A healer’s kit succeeds automatically but consumes one use.
Resurrection restores life but does not automatically remove Wounds, Corruption, debt, legal death, or claims upon the recovered body.
Retreat or injury
Take damage equal to proficiency bonus at the end of each turn. An action and Medicine check or magical healing ends it.
Disadvantage on precise Dexterity and Intelligence checks; advantage on one save against fear. Stacks worsen into Dazed and Unconscious.
